messages:
maria: Thanks everyone for the all-hands — quick follow-up thread on the customer win/loss patterns we surfaced. I pulled together the top themes and a few clarifying Qs for leadership. TL;DR — wins were onboarding speed, clear migration playbooks, and predictable perf; losses clustered around integration friction (KMS/HSM), SLA expectations, and edge-case model quality. Questions below, please react and assign owners.

sam: Appreciate the summary, +1 on those themes. High level answers: we prioritize pipeline that converts to committed revenue (reserved/dedicated). That means SLA+Private signals will get bumped if there's clear revenue. We're accelerating Private GA timeline and aligning SLA tiers. More specifics coming from Alex/Eng. :raised_hands:

alex: Engineering context: quantization/ft-speedups are high-impact for cost. Current estimate: 6–8 weeks for an initial quantized build for our 30B family (engineering caveats). Immediate P0s are (1) canonical perf benchmark suite for typical seq lengths, (2) KV cache telemetry + regression alerts. We'll need product to lock the eval prompt sets.

jordan: From sales: customers that signed had a concrete migration runbook and token-cost transparency. We lost deals when KMS/HSM or SOC2 timelines weren't nailed down, or when latency SLOs weren't explicit. Top asks we hear repeatedly: on-prem option, token cost per-route, SLA for p99 latency, and formal onboarding playbooks.

tina: Re: canary/rollouts — we need a small cross-functional plan: metrics (latency, error-rate, token-cost delta), safety gates, and rollback steps. I can own the rollout checklist if someone owns the playbook content (onboarding checklist + migration steps).

maria: Can leadership confirm who will own: (A) Private GA timeline & SLA packaging, (B) onboarding playbook content, (C) quantization/perf priority. If ownership already exists, please @ them and we'll track. Also requesting a short customer-facing FAQ template we can give AE teams.

sam: I'll own (A) and coordinate with legal/security for KMS/HSM requirements. Alex will lead (C) with Eng. Jordan/CS should drive (B) with product help. We'll get a single-page FAQ from comms next week.

alex: Confirming I own (C). Tina — please pair on rollout checklist and perf metrics. Maria — can product drop the eval prompt sets by EOD Friday? We'll need them to validate quantized builds.

maria: Yes — I'll upload the eval sets and example traffic profiles to the shared doc. Also creating an action doc now with owners, timeline, and acceptance criteria. Link: https://redwood.app/docs/all-hands/customer-followup (placeholder).

jordan: Can we include two sales-ready bullet points for each lost deal: 1) what was missing, 2) what we can offer next quarter. I can draft a template and share.

tina: I'll make a short checklist gist for the canary and perf gates, and post it here once done.

ops-bot: Created issue #1234 in ops/redwood-customer-playbooks: "All-hands follow-up — customer playbook + SLA alignment" assigned to sam, alex, maria.

maria: Awesome — thanks everyone. Action items: sam (Private+SLA), alex/tina (quant+rollout), jordan/CS (playbook drafts), maria (evals + doc). Let's sync Thurs 10a for 30m. If anyone needs to be looped in, reply here. :calendar:
